steps.text: 13 Years Ago
8:09 P.M. \ Heavy snow
Victoria Border Autonomous Region, County of Toron, Vincent Manor

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: It is a great city. All Victorians should find time to pay it a visit and gaze upon its magnificence.

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: So you are saying our respectable dukes have not yet arrived at a conclusion?

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Yes, that is correct. They haven't yet. For the time being, Londinium is still a city without a master.

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: So I take it you had the fortune and privilege to tour Londinium with the Duke of Normandy?

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Alas, the Duke is forbidden from entering Londinium by law. Of course, he is a fine gentleman, so he would never be so presumptuous as to invite himself in, so we instead enjoyed dinner on a ship together in the Londinium countryside.

steps.name: Tipsy Businessman
steps.text: What kind of a hero is the Duke?

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Well... he is the most gracious and erudite of nobles. His views in economics and politics are unique and unparalleled. Not only that, but my understanding is that he is well-trained in music, and he possesses an impressive art collection, testament to his respect for the arts.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: It is because of heroes like him that Victoria remains prosperous as ever!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Despite not having a ruler for the past dozen or so years, Victoria has managed to maintain its stability.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: But the truth is that the Dukes were getting in each other's way behind the scenes, and that's not all...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: If so many Victorian nobles actually fell victim to food poisoning and hunting accidents, then the country's noble rule would've crumbled to dust long ago.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And three years ago, your father nearly experienced that first hand.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Yes...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: His leg is actually injured.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: There is a noble who is an academic enemy of my father. They were at a cocktail party together, and he made his move after the party.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That must have been well disguised, if it was thought to be an accident.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: My father had a few leads, but he didn't want this affair to get in the way of relaying intelligence.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: How many of Thomson's men are there in this manor right now?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: A lot of them, such as the ones you were talking to earlier... They also paid my father's villa a visit before tonight's party.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Richard was quite critical of your father just now...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Ahaha... I suppose he spoke much of it from his heart... He has had quite the rivalry with my father for the past several years...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Yet they still assemble around Thomson. Your father is a good leader.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Not without your guidance, Lady Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Who could have thought back then... that the Laterano cleric who came to visit Victoria would become our most trusted mentor?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Our goals are one and the same.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Kal'tsit. They will get out of this unscathed... We will get out of this unscathed, will we?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Heidi...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You need to look around with your own eyes. If you truly wish to step into this world, then you cannot allow civilization's facades blind you anymore... You need to see this world yourself.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Comforting words are meaningless. You will grow up one day.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Now, unpleasant as it may be, I must say I heard a rumor from the lesser nobles and ruffians...

steps.name: Merry Noblewoman
steps.text: My, did they upset you?

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: Right... As you can see, it was the Dukes' graciousness that forged the peace and prosperity enjoyed by our country today.

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: However, and this is something that even the traitors in Columbia are aware of, we also cannot deny that it has been a long time since Victoria has seen a rightful ruler ascend its throne.

steps.name: Pretentious Man
steps.text: And what of it? Does that not go to show we are becoming ever more powerful through our own means?

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: You are correct, Richard, but there was also this opinion... It was naive and absurd... There was this crowd of men there each with their own goals...

steps.name: Count Vincent
steps.text: They asked if Victoria truly needed a new ruler.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: They all said Uncle Vincent's too much of a coward...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: We're near the border, but we are being so complacent, not making any progress... This is our chance to fight for our rights... yet all Uncle Vincent knows to do is throwing parties in the manor.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Even this trip to Londinium. It hardly achieved any meaningful results.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This isn't your father's opinion. Thomson is not so foolish as to let radical atmosphere get to his head.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: But that's how the adults always complain to my father.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No foolish nobles would ever receive an audience with a real Duke.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Do you think that the Duke of Normandy really didn't intimidate Vincent with any harsh demands?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Toron is near the border, and there are few people here. In other words, this place is not under the influence of any major forces.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Uncle Vincent...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This nobleman may seem uninterested in anything except celebrating this false peace with music and shows, but he is actually doing his best to uphold Toron's peace. That's despite the peace here... is fragile and easily broken.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: His arrogance and temperance are just at the right level to hide his thoughts well, and those who actually understand his true intentions are few and far between.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Thomson would never place so much trust on a count severely lacking in courage, insight, and judgement. They may seem like they are heading down different paths, but these paths will lead them to the same destination.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Hehe... It's nice to hear you say so.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Kal'tsit, are you not going to look at your mail?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: From Londinium to Toron, these letters have made it halfway across Victoria.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: How many hands has the letter passed through, and how many of them know of the whole truth of these events?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: There are lots—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Workers, newsboys, popcorn hawkers, park gardeners. They knew nothing of the letter's contents. They didn't even know who these words ultimately belong to.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But now this letter has made it to Thomson, and now me.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There is nothing to worry about.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I see...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: But what about the other one? The one from 'Kazdel'...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It was handed straight to Thomson by a Sarkaz Messenger.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I told him how to contact Thomson himself, but if things had gone according to plan, he would've handed this straight to me.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Yeah... but when that Sarkaz made it to Victoria...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Father did not know how the Sarkaz honor their heroes' death, so all we could do was cremate his body according to our traditions and scatter his ashes in the nomadic city's waterways.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I can't tell you his real name, but, at the very least, he died as a Messenger, and I will bring his story back to his homeland.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: He won't be forgotten.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Kal'tsit... Is this how you treat everyone?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Why do you ask?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: No, I was just thinking... Ah... Aaah...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Achoo!

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Oh! P-Pardon me... How unbecoming of me...!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The snow is getting heavier. Let's head back inside.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I will pay Thomson a visit once this party is over.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I am sure Father will be happy.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Should I perhaps hold your arm? That way no one will be suspicious of us.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If you think that is necessary.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Okay... Hehe, you're so much taller than me.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You haven't grown at all, Heidi.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Take a look outside, Kal'tsit. The snow is so heavy. I haven't seen this much snow in a very long time.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You are right. A snowstorm is coming.

a.text: Heidi ponders to herself: Just how many clouds are needed to shed so many snowflakes?
The white snow is scattering in all directions, gyrating into the sky as the wind blows past.
Where the pale yellow lights cannot illuminate has been shrouded in a thick mist that covers the entire city.
The night sky tonight is without stars and moonlight.
The black tidal wave is beginning to crash upon the beaches.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Kal'tsit?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Black snow...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Huh? I'm not seeing any...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Heidi, tell everyone to keep the party venue under control.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I need about an hour's time. Don't let anyone near the garden...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I can do that... but what's going on with you all of a sudden?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We've got company.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: We may be on the border, but this manor belongs to a Victorian count! Who would—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: —Heidi, if I don't come back to the manor, you and your father need to keep this secret.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Do not dig any deeper into this.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: But—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This is a warning as well as an order.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Be safe.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: To the north of Sami and Ursus and to the south of Sargon... Those lands yet untrodden by man...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Whether the demons and monsters that dwell there are normal creatures is yet unknown, but they are far older than any country we know.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Humans have fought them for a long time. Indeed, this is a proposition worthy of further notice.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Until now...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Humans can now be the masters of their own countries.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The ancient Sargon king and the powerful Kheshigs hit it off right away, and the Nightzmora's Khagan strove to conquer all lands unexplored by civilization.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The results were impressive. No non-human threat ever set foot in Sargon territory again.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Sami has used countless witchcrafts and sacrifices to create their Snowpriests, and, one generation after another, the sorceresses lost themselves as they battled the enemies from beyond their borders.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And Ursus—You deployed the strongest elites to simply tear them to shreds. Wendigos in heavy armor or veteran war Casters.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And the Empire's ambitions are without limit. Your kind did not merely tear them to shreds.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You used the shreds of power left behind by those non-humans.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Show yourself.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The will of Ursus drove you here.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You are far underestimating Victoria's might. The aura of demons lingers in your footsteps. Have you ever given any thought to where your responsibility lies?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your mind can't already be taken by the demons, Royal Guard.

a.text: As the figure steps out into the light, the unilluminated darkness surrounding it begins to quiver.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: I can smell the fear in you, traitor.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It took you a while to find me.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: If it wasn't for the uprising and its aftermath, I would've come to lay down your punishment long ago.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: The imbeciles allowed you to escape. This has been an embarrassment, and they have already been executed for their incompetence.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Perhaps I should remind you again. The snowstorm here can bury entire cities, but they cannot erase the footsteps of a Royal Guard.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You are in Victoria, and there stands the manor of a Victorian count not a hundred meters behind me.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Do you understand the consequences of your actions—

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: —Consequences?

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: Your threat is weak and empty. Wherever I stand, the earth beneath me belongs to the Empire of Ursus.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: You never had the right to address me, traitor, not before the word 'demon' left your lips. Soon, I will beat out of you how you came to know this secret...

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: Your understanding of the 'demons' does not grant you a dialogue. You murdered an Ursus Grand Duke, and you know of our darkest secrets.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: Your countless crimes... are worthy of a thousand deaths.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It seems we won't be convincing each other for the moment.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Though that applies only to... your evaluation of the situation on hand.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: Beast, bare your fangs!

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: You can't fool me!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Mon3tr...

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Impatient braying)

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Mon3tr, do not underestimate him.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: He's no normal human.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: You hid a device here in the garden... No... a creature...? *Hiss*...

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: You know of the 'demons,' and you have a monster serving you. One that Ursus's vast knowledge is yet unaware of.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: Perhaps your crimes have far exceeded my expectations.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Or perhaps I managed to make an impression on a Royal Guard.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: *Hiss*...!

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: I won't deny it, traitor.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: But you have my curiosity. What drove you to betray our homeland...? No, no... Perhaps... my investigations did not fully uncover your entire past.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: And it looks like that is indeed the case. Unlike the criminals who escaped to Sami, it appears you still have a trick up your sleeve.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: Do not get the wrong idea... It is hardly a difficult matter... to kill you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I suppose it's why you are staining this area around us?

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: You needn't concern yourself. I know what I am doing.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: —Mon3tr!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Wailing)—

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: *Hiss*... I did not expect it to be this hard.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: If your own flesh and blood is also as hardened, then, indeed, it makes you a formidable foe.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Mon3tr, come back. Don't chase after him.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Avoid the black mist. That's not mist at all.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This is far beyond the normal realm of Originium Arts... It looks like it has really been too long since I last dealt with the Emperor's Blade. You and your men have made remarkable progress.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: You know this much about our secrets...?!

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: Even the most senior Ursus scientist would never be allowed to meddle in the Royal Guards' ancient ritual...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Ancient rituals. Yes, only the ceremonies of your crazed, self-proclaimed spiritual leaders could adorn your kinds with your demons.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You're a survivor of the Valley of the Setting Sun.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: *Hiss*...!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Empire's will is always focused and unswerving, yet your goal seems to stray from your motherland's. At the very least, you are not that young.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You should not be fighting me, Royal Guard. Both you and I know that the job I finished was one that you and your men should've done yourselves, but never did.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: Don't be mistaken about where that right lies, traitor. You do not represent Deity Grypherburg's laws and prestige.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If you truly witnessed the whole uprising, Royal Guard, then you should understand this more so than anyone. The Empire's rise and fall has never truly been affected by dignity and honor.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Let me ask you this, then. Did the last emperor ever truly look down on Victoria from the bottom of his heart?

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: Perhaps I do not give you enough credit, traitor.

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: I will give you one last chance. Reveal your secrets, and I will grant you a dignified death.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Alas, given this death would have nothing to do with my own conviction, dignity was never on the table.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Mon3tr.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Elated braying)

steps.name: 'Emperor's Blade'
steps.text: *Hiss*... *Huff*...
As the fear in the air heightens, the Royal Guard draws his blade. He is about to execute Ursus's will.
